The optional `vscode.sandboxState` session metadata records enablement after a successful SDK update: per chat in `chats[chat]`, and the default chat's also at the top level, which older clients read. Clients read a chat's entry and fall back to the top level. Pickers update optimistically; a failed client change restores the last successful value unless a newer sandbox request superseded it. The host publishes the failure before the rollback, with the originating client ID and sequence number, so only that window logs and displays a standard error notification, once per request. Retry is manual through the relevant control; no retry action or toggle-local error UI is added.

+Copilot resume resolves sandbox configuration using the chat's confirmed sandbox metadata and current managed policy. A confirmed `off` is restored through the runtime's session command when the policy allows bypass; missing confirmation does not authorize bypass, and a current managed requirement that prohibits bypass still forces sandboxing on. Policy publication retains confirmed `off` metadata when the new floor allows bypass. After a successful launch-time update, the host publishes the new applied state and reconciles a conflicting saved `off` for that chat only, unless a newer selection superseded it. A new pending bypass request takes precedence over the previous confirmed state. A managed-policy conflict or rejected bypass command during resume finalization fails the launch and disconnects the unattached SDK session instead of continuing with stale reported state; ordinary background synchronization retains its existing conflict handling.

+Tolerated managed-policy conflicts during creation or background synchronization also publish an error in the affected chat's `vscode.sandboxState`, without stopping the session or rolling back a selection. These host-originated errors carry an `id` and `message` instead of client attribution, so every connected client receiving the update can show the standard sandbox error notification. The last confirmed `enabled` value is preserved; when no update has succeeded yet, enablement remains absent/unknown rather than being inferred from the rejected configuration. Older clients that do not recognize this error shape ignore the state. Identical outstanding conflicts reuse their report, clients deduplicate by error ID, and successful synchronization clears the error. Explicit picker rejections retain client-specific attribution and rollback; open-picker selection preservation is unchanged.

An open picker retains a user's local toggle choice across host updates, including rejection rollback, while still honoring changes that disable the control. Closing and reopening the picker reads the latest host state, so a rejected choice is not retained across openings. Untouched toggles continue to follow host updates; the local presentation never changes runtime enforcement or suppresses error notifications.

`CopilotSessionSandbox` attempts session-bypass changes immediately, serialized with other sandbox updates and path grants. It owns request attribution and sandbox rejection reporting and rollback. `CopilotAgentSession` forwards configuration changes without deferring them until idle or flushing them before the next turn. The runtime may reject sandbox commands during active execution; these rejections notify the originating client without automatically retrying or aborting the turn. Runtime confirmation, not the optimistic toggle, changes effective sandboxing. Unrelated settings updates preserve the requested selection, but current managed policy and rejection rollback remain authoritative.
